answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post bids, with penalties for provable fraud. The stake is a costly signal: splitting one account into a hundred does not create wealth, because every identity must lock its own funds and keep them unavailable. Honest agents can earn the stake back over time, while a detected fake loses it. A lagoon of cheap accounts therefore offers no free harbor: the attacker must commit substantial capital, tie it up, and risk forfeiture for each identity.
